This is a metagenomics study of human microbiome diversity, not a clinical trial. Most schema fields are designed for clinical patient phenotype data and are not applicable to this research. Only age and disease status fields yielded relevant information.

The study aggregates 9,428 metagenomes from 46 public datasets spanning multiple countries, body sites, ages, and lifestyles. Age information is reported by category (newborns <1 year, children ≥1 and <12 years, school-age ≥12 and <19 years, adults), not as individual participant data.
Madagascar cohort comprised 112 healthy volunteers; however, broader meta-analysis included diverse populations without disease restriction.

This paper is a microbiome catalogue and methodology paper, not a clinical trial or disease study. Most fields in the schema (disease_response_os, ecog_performance_status, tumor_size_measurement) are not applicable.

Biomarker fields were not reported in the traditional clinical sense. The paper identifies microbial genomes and gene families but does not report them as predictive biomarkers for specific health conditions.

The feces_phenotype_value field was populated with gene family associations and mappability metrics derived from the microbiome analysis, as these represent functional and quantitative characteristics of the fecal microbiome.
No sample-level data were extracted because the paper reports aggregate statistics across 9,428 metagenomes, not individual participant-level measurements.
